title: Sunshine Pictures IPO Subscribed 4.33 Times on Day 1 as Investors Bet on Bollywood Producer
excerpt: The Vipul Shah-promoted production house behind Holiday and Commando sees strong opening-day demand for its ₹282-crore mainboard offering.
body:
• Sunshine Pictures, the production house behind films like Holiday and Commando, opened its ₹282-crore IPO on August 18 with a price band of ₹342–360 per share.
  • The offering was 4.33 times subscribed on Day 1, with strong interest from non-institutional and retail investors.
  • Promoters Vipul Amrutlal Shah and Shefali Vipul Shah are selling 30.37 lakh shares through the offer for sale component.
  • At the upper price band, the company is valued at approximately ₹1,121 crore. Listing on BSE and NSE is expected on August 25.

Bollywood Production House Draws Strong Day 1 Demand

Sunshine Pictures Ltd, the film and web series production company promoted by producer-director Vipul Amrutlal Shah, saw its ₹282-crore initial public offering subscribed 4.33 times on the first day of bidding, August 18. The mainboard IPO, priced at ₹342–360 per share with a face value of ₹10, will remain open for subscription until August 20.

The strong opening day subscription signals investor appetite for content production companies despite the sector's inherent project-to-project revenue volatility. Non-institutional investors and retail bidders drove much of the demand, according to exchange data.

"IPO Structure The offering comprises a fresh issue of 48 lakh equity shares and an offer for sale of 30.37 lakh shares, bringing the total to 78.37 lakh shares."

IPO Structure

The offering comprises a fresh issue of 48 lakh equity shares and an offer for sale of 30.37 lakh shares, bringing the total to 78.37 lakh shares. Promoters Vipul Amrutlal Shah and Shefali Vipul Shah are selling 20.31 lakh and 10.06 lakh shares respectively through the OFS.

Sunshine Pictures plans to deploy up to ₹112.50 crore from the fresh issue proceeds toward long-term working capital requirements, with the remainder earmarked for general corporate purposes. At the upper end of the price band, the company carries an implied post-issue market capitalisation of approximately ₹1,121 crore.

GYR Capital Advisors Private Ltd is the book-running lead manager, while Bigshare Services Private Ltd serves as registrar. The basis of allotment is expected on August 21, with listing on both BSE and NSE scheduled for August 25.

The Company Behind the IPO

Sunshine Pictures is engaged in originating, developing, producing, marketing, and distributing films and web series. The company's production credits include commercial Bollywood films such as Holiday: A Soldier Is Never Off Duty, the Commando franchise, and Namaste England, alongside television serials and web series.

The production house has completed 10 commercial films — six of them co-produced with other studios — along with two web series, two television serials, and one short commercial film. Its current pipeline includes two films being co-produced with Jio Studios and a web series for state broadcaster Prasar Bharati, streaming on Doordarshan and its OTT platform. Eight additional films and two web series are in various stages of development.

Investor Allocation and Grey Market Premium

Of the total issue, 50% is reserved for qualified institutional buyers, 15% for non-institutional investors, and 35% for retail investors. The minimum application size is 41 shares, requiring an investment of ₹14,760 at the upper price band.

In the grey market, Sunshine Pictures shares were trading at an estimated premium of ₹78 per share, or roughly 21.67% above the upper band price, according to IPO tracking platforms — suggesting expectations of a positive listing.

What to Watch

Content production IPOs in India have had a mixed track record. Investors will be evaluating whether Sunshine Pictures can deliver consistent revenue visibility from its development pipeline rather than relying on the box-office performance of individual releases. The company's ability to secure co-production deals with established studios like Jio Studios and distribution through Prasar Bharati suggests a diversified revenue approach, though the entertainment sector remains fundamentally hit-driven.
